name: Krishak Praja Party
contribution: Founded in 1936 under A.K. Fazlul Huq, the party carried tenant and peasant demands into electoral politics through an anti-zamindari, anti-mahajan program.
context: The Krishak Praja Party grew out of the All Bengal Tenants’ Association and contested the first Bengal provincial election under the Government of India Act of 1935. Its 1937 success helped Fazlul Huq form a coalition ministry, even as the party’s rural program and later relationship with the Muslim League generated tensions.
impact: The party made agrarian grievances, rural representation, debt relief, and tenancy reform central to Bengal’s provincial political debate. Its short-lived organization also shows the limits of translating peasant-oriented promises into stable coalition government before partition.
highlight: Fazlul Huq’s 1930s peasant-tenant party that brought agrarian demands into Bengal’s provincial legislature.
seoTitle: Krishak Praja Party: Bengal’s Peasant-Tenant Political Movement
seoDescription: Learn about the Krishak Praja Party, A.K. Fazlul Huq’s 1936 Bengal party, its agrarian program, and its role in the 1937 provincial coalition government.
shortAnswer: The Krishak Praja Party was a Bengal peasant-tenant party founded in 1936 under A.K. Fazlul Huq that contested zamindari power and shaped the 1937 provincial government.

faq.question: When was the Krishak Praja Party founded?
faq.answer: It was founded in 1936 under A.K. Fazlul Huq, emerging from the All Bengal Tenants’ Association.

faq.question: What did the Krishak Praja Party stand for?
faq.answer: Its platform emphasized peasant and tenant interests, including opposition to zamindari power, relief from agricultural debt, and tenancy reform.
